title: Labs are aware that AI is undercutting the web it runs on, court records show - TCR 09/18/26
description:
Unsealed New York Times case filings show a Microsoft director calling AI scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history' and internal documents warning of a 'doom loop' that cut publisher click-throughs up to 93 percent, Google, Nvidia and Anthropic launched an AI Energy Management Alliance to free 100 gigawatts of grid capacity by pausing noncritical compute, and the Chinese lab Z.ai reported a GLM-5.3 agent built its successor's production inference system in under two weeks.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-18-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:40 Microsoft and OpenAI's own 'theft' filings
3:26 A grid coalition frees 100 GW without new plants
6:07 A model helps build its successor's inference system
8:52 Novo turns to Claude for drug discovery
11:23 Scotland, South Africa, and the House 417-3 vote
14:06 Close

This episode covers the unsealed Microsoft and OpenAI 'theft of labor' filings and the content doom loop, the Google-Nvidia-Anthropic AI Energy Management Alliance and Emerald AI, Z.ai's GLM-5.3 infrastructure agent, Novo Nordisk's Claude Science drug-discovery partnership, Scotland's data-center pause and the US House's 417-3 ratepayer vote, and the DOE's $215 million quantum computing competition.

A brief unsealed in the New York Times copyright case surfaced internal correspondence, including a Microsoft director calling mass scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history' and an internal presentation warning of a 'doom loop' where publisher click-throughs fell as much as 93 percent after the answer engine drew on their reporting. The filing describes engineers stripping copyright notices before training data reached the model and an OpenAI cofounder answering a flagged paywall workaround with 'ah nice.' The same week, Google, Nvidia and Anthropic joined utilities in an AI Energy Management Alliance to free 100 gigawatts of grid capacity by pausing noncritical compute, and Z.ai reported a GLM-5.3 agent built the production inference system that will train its successor in under two weeks. Novo Nordisk pointed Claude Science at drug discovery after a 20 percent share slide, a Stanford spinout ran a virtual biotech of 37,000 AI agents, and three governments - Scotland, South Africa, and the US House at 417 to 3 - moved to make data centers pay for the power and water their demand draws. The DOE opened a $215 million quantum computing competition.
